_transcription: PAGE MAP: the booklet is 12 rendered pages (idx 0-11 = printed folios 1-12), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB3/1, SET-1, Q.P. Code 57/1/1, BIOLOGY (Theory), 2 hours, 35 marks, 12 printed pages, 13 questions). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The tops of all five odd indices were checked in one full-width montage: each opens in Hindi (idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 3 Hindi Q5, idx 5 Hindi Section B / Q7, idx 7 Hindi Q11, idx 9 Hindi Q13 sub-parts), so NO English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion. idx 11 (folio 12) is BLANK at full size (a rule, an asterisk, the footer); at thumbnail size it shows scanner show-through of folio 11, which is NOT content. The paper is a pure scan, read by vision only. Structure as printed: Section A Q1-6 @2, Section B Q7-12 @3, Section C Q13 case-based @5 = 35. Instruction (iv) says internal choices exist but gives no count; the roster was built from the scheme's bare ORs and each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper: Q2, Q6, Q12 and Q13 (four alternatives). The Q13 OR replaces the WHOLE case study (its alternative is a standalone 5-mark question with no reference to the passage), so it is one row Q13b alternative to Q13ai, the shape used by 2023 55/2/1 Q34b; the four case sub-parts carry the scheme's split 2/1/1/1. Quotes straightened (Q6 OR and Q11 print curly double quotes), scientific names plain (Anopheles, Plasmodium; Q12(ii) prints 'E.coli' underlined, carried as plain text). Typos kept as printed: Q5(b) 'could have lead', Q8(a) 'have already taken', Q13 passage 'which produces cry-proteins ... Thus saves', Q13(iii) 'advise'. No question asks the student to draw, so no _drawFigure.

questions.stem: Mention the parts of human body that get affected by Pneumonia and common cold infections. Write the causative agents of the two diseases.
State the impact of constant mechanical agitation and pumping of air in the aeration tank on the sewage during the biological treatment.

(a) Cattle excreta is important source for producing a domestic fuel. Name the fuel and write its main components.
(b) Write the biological process that is responsible for the production of this fuel.

(a) Give an example of viral biocontrol agent.
(b) Why are they considered to be desirable when an ecologically sensitive area is being treated ?
What is the importance of female Anopheles mosquitoes in the life of a malarial Parasite Plasmodium ?

Study the graph given below, showing the population growth curves 'A' and 'B' respectively. Answer the following questions :
(a) What is 'Carrying Capacity' in respect of Curve 'B' indicative of ?
(b) Mention the action of possible natural forces that could have lead to curve 'B'.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a graph of Population size (y) against Time / Generation (x) with a dashed horizontal line marked Carrying Capacity and two curves labelled 'A' and 'B' rising from the origin, the region between them shaded; which curve has which shape (and so which growth model each is) is decided by the drawing and is withheld here. Page idx 4.

questions.stem:
The histogram given below representing the data for annual shark harvest in the great barrier reef / coral reef located on the east coast of Queensland, Australia. Study the histogram and answer the questions that follow.
(a) Write your interpretation of the data given.
(b) Write the impact on the biodiversity of the area that you can interpret on the basis of given data.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a histogram of Catch (tonnes), axis 0 to 1200, for each year 1992 to 2003, with the caption 'Source : Fijisharkdiving.blogspot.com'; the bar heights carry the trend the question asks the student to interpret, so they are withheld here. Page idx 4.

questions.stem: "Stability of community depends upon its species richness." How did David Tilman show this experimentally ?

questions.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
questions.stem:
The data collected based on the survey conducted for species richness of group of mammals, in three different climatic regions of the world is shown in the bar graph given below.
Panama has nearly 560 species of mammals, Canada has nearly 301 species of mammals and Denmark has 67 species of mammals.
(i) Based on the species, richness, identify the location of these countries in the respective climatic regions given.
(ii) Plants and animals do not have a uniform diversity in the world. Write the term given to this pattern of diversity and why ?
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a bar graph of Taxonomic Richness (y, increasing upward from 0) for three bars labelled Polar (N) region, Temperate (N) region and Tropic region; the relative bar heights decide which country goes with which region, so they are withheld here. Page idx 6.

questions.stem:
Bio-diversification of life started to occur almost 3 billion years ago. Since then new species have been evolving and then disappearing en masse from earth.
(a) How many episodes of mass extinctions of species have already taken place and which one is in progress in the current era ?
(b) How is current episode in progress different from the previous episodes and why ? Explain.

Name two naturally occurring sources, one that transfers pathogenic genes into a plant cells and the other into an animal cell respectively, for their benefit. Write how have these naturally occurring sources been used for the benefit of human race by the biotechnologists.
Enumerate the main sources of bio-fertilisers giving one example of each.
Explain giving reason the action plan followed by organic farmers that support their key belief "biodiversity furthers health of crop lands".

(i) State the role of a selectable marker in r-DNA technology.
(ii) Name one such selectable marker which is considered to be useful for E.coli.
(iii) Give one reason why is it considered to be a useful marker.
What are plasmids ? How are they different from cloning vectors ? Give one example each for a viral and a bacterial cloning vector.

questions.context: To save the crop plant from the attack of various insect pests the biotechnologists have developed many pest resistant plants. One such example is Bt corn plant. In this plant 'cry' genes were introduced which produces cry-proteins in the plant that has toxic effect on the pest (corn borer). Thus saves the corn plant from the attack of the corn borer. An experimental field study was conducted by the scientists to see the efficacy of the Bt corn plant against the attack of corn borers. Three different species of corn borers namely 'A', 'B', 'C' were collected and were independently fed on non Bt corn plants and Bt corn plants separately for the same period. The extent of the damage caused to the leaf area of the plant was observed and noted down. With the help of the observations and data collected the following bar graph was plotted. Study the graph and answer the questions that follow.
questions.stem: Identify the species of the corn borer that was most successfully controlled by Bt corn plant. Give appropriate reason for your inference.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a bar graph of % of leaf area damaged / mm² (y, 0 to 80) for two groups, Non-Bt Crop and Bt Crop, each with one bar per corn-borer species keyed A (diagonal hatching), B (vertical lines) and C (open); the bar heights decide which species is best controlled, so they are withheld here. Page idx 8.

questions.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
questions.stem: A gene was identified in a fungus by a research worker in a lab which was considered to be of a great importance in the field of agriculture. As a student of biotechnology, write the steps you would suggest to (i) Isolate this gene of interest from the fungus and (ii) amplify this gene for further experimentation and research.
